rule: One row per example literal per recipe, read by hand from the pinned overlay. The literal is the exact text in the published command and must still occur there, or the row is stale and the test says so. It becomes `<param>` (or `becomes`, when fixed text surrounds it) before classification, so the classifier sees an unbound placeholder where a stranger's account id was. Reserved names (ACCOUNT_ID, PARTITION, REGION, WINDOW_START, WINDOW_END, EPOCH_START, EPOCH_END) are bound by the appliance at request time; every other name is the config's `aws.params` to supply. Left as published, on purpose: AWS-managed Config rule names, the AWS-managed `SSM-SessionManagerRunShell` document, Shield's `--region us-east-1` (its API endpoint, not an example), and the `guardduty`/`SecurityHub` name prefixes on two list calls (filters whose empty result is a `0 of 0` population the evaluator already distinguishes).
